rigor.explanation: Two unsupported steps chained together: that a stated commitment produces investment certainty, and that investment certainty 'will ensure' emissions reductions. Nothing is offered to connect either link, and 'ensure' claims more than the premises allow.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Very much—we’re going to be very straight up with the New Zealand people, and what they have heard today is that that was a previous Government that led three of the last four quarters’ declining economic growth.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that three of the four most recent quarters recorded declining GDP, and that these fell under the previous Government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ national accounts, quarterly real GDP growth for the four quarters to the September 2023 quarter; true if three of those four quarters show a fall, false if two or fewer do.

veracity.statement: What they’ve heard today, and we’ve been straight up with the New Zealand people about, is a $15 billion New Zealand Upgrade project with an Auditor-General’s report that says it was appallingly managed—appallingly managed.
veracity.explanation: Two assertions: that the New Zealand Upgrade Programme is a $15 billion programme, and that the Auditor-General's report characterises its management as appalling.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Office of the Auditor-General's report on the New Zealand Upgrade Programme, plus the programme's announced budget; true if the report finds serious management failures and the programme's value is around $15 billion, false if the report makes no such finding or the announced value is materially lower (the programme was announced at $6.8b and later restated at $8.7b).

veracity.statement: But what I’d just say: I think it is ironic on a day when we’ve had economic news where in three of the last quarters under the previous Government we had negative economic growth, at a time when inflation has been out of the band for the last over 21 months, when we’ve seen wages not keeping pace with inflation, we haven’t had a single economic question from the Opposition—a single economic question from the Opposition.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that annual inflation has been outside the Reserve Bank's target band for more than 21 consecutive months.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ CPI annual inflation against the RBNZ 1–3% target band for each quarter to December 2023; true if annual CPI sat above 3% for more than 21 consecutive months, false if the run is shorter.

veracity.statement: Does he stand by his Government’s decision to repeal fair pay agreements, the Reserve Bank dual mandate, and the Clean Car Discount under urgency with no select committee process or regulatory impact statement, or does he agree with Chris Bishop that “This is a disgraceful way to make important law.”?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the three named measures were repealed under urgency without select committee or regulatory impact statement, and that Chris Bishop said the quoted words about law-making by urgency.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Hansard for the December 2023 urgency motions covering the Fair Pay Agreements, Reserve Bank dual mandate and Clean Car Discount repeals (true if no select committee stage occurred), plus the Hansard or media record of Chris Bishop's remarks; false if he did not say the quoted words.

veracity.statement: Does the Government now support the immediate humanitarian ceasefire it voted for at the United Nations General Assembly yesterday, or does it still believe there are a list of preconditions that must be met before calling for a ceasefire?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand voted in favour of the immediate humanitarian ceasefire resolution at the UN General Assembly on the previous day.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The UN General Assembly voting record for the emergency special session resolution of 12 December 2023 demanding an immediate humanitarian ceasefire; true if New Zealand is recorded voting in favour, false if it abstained or voted against.

veracity.statement: Statistics New Zealand confirmed today that GDP declined in the third quarter of this year, a third decline in just the last year.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a Stats NZ release showing a September-quarter GDP fall, and that this is the third quarterly fall within the last year.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ gross domestic product release for the September 2023 quarter and the preceding three quarters; true if the September quarter fell and three of the last four quarters fell, false otherwise.

veracity.statement: I’ve also seen reports from the member for Remutaka, who claimed last week that we “inherited an economy that is growing faster than many economists had predicted” and that the economy was “never in recession”, but I have seen no evidence to confirm those reports.
veracity.explanation: Relays a claim attributed to another member — that the economy was never in recession and was growing faster than economists predicted — and disputes it. What is at issue is the accuracy of the relayed claim.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ quarterly GDP for the December 2022 and March 2023 quarters; the relayed 'never in recession' claim is true if there were not two consecutive quarterly declines, false if there were. Also requires a record of the member's remarks in the week to 12 December 2023.

veracity.statement: Today’s GDP per capita figures show on a per person basis the New Zealand economy has gone nowhere since the start of 2021 and has gone backwards four quarters in a row.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that GDP per capita fell in each of the four quarters to September 2023 and that the level is no higher than at the start of 2021.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ GDP per capita series; true if it records four consecutive quarterly declines to the September 2023 quarter and a level at or below the March 2021 quarter, false if either leg fails.

veracity.statement: I note that the Boston Consulting Group study The Future is Electric found that electrification could reduce annual carbon emissions by 22 million tonnes in 2050.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a named Boston Consulting Group report found electrification could cut annual emissions by 22 million tonnes by 2050.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Boston Consulting Group report 'The Future is Electric'; true if it contains a finding of approximately 22 Mt annual CO2e abatement in 2050 from electrification, false if the figure or the year is materially different.

veracity.statement: Can he confirm that the percentage of New Zealand’s greenhouse gas emissions that come from the electricity generation is 5.7 percent, whereas the percentage of New Zealand’s greenhouse gas emissions that come from the energy sector is 40.6 percent?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that electricity generation accounts for 5.7% and the energy sector for 40.6% of New Zealand's greenhouse gas emissions.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: New Zealand's Greenhouse Gas Inventory (Ministry for the Environment) for the most recent reported year; true if electricity generation is approximately 5.7% and the energy sector approximately 40.6% of gross emissions, false if either share is materially different.

veracity.statement: What is his plan to fix market imbalances in an electricity market dominated by four gentailers, which today’s Generating Scarcity 2023 report shows has stifled investment in renewable electricity generation and resulted in billions of excess dividends to shareholders, all while thousands of New Zealanders struggle to heat their homes?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a named report released that day finds gentailer dominance has stifled renewable generation investment and produced billions in excess dividends.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The 'Generating Scarcity 2023' report; true if it contains findings that the four-gentailer structure suppressed renewable generation investment and quantifies excess dividends in the billions, false if it makes no such findings or the magnitude is materially smaller.

focus.statement: But what I’d just say: I think it is ironic on a day when we’ve had economic news where in three of the last quarters under the previous Government we had negative economic growth, at a time when inflation has been out of the band for the last over 21 months, when we’ve seen wages not keeping pace with inflation, we haven’t had a single economic question from the Opposition—a single economic question from the Opposition.
focus.explanation: Economic figures are cited, but the point being made is about what the Opposition chose to ask rather than about the measure or decision at issue. The weight of the statement is on the other team's conduct.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: That Government over there wanted to subsidise wealthy businesses with profitable businesses using taxpayers’ money.
focus.explanation: There is a genuine policy point here — decarbonisation subsidies to industry — but it is delivered as a characterisation of what the other side wanted rather than as an engagement with the process-heat question asked. A real policy claim wrapped in party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I think our position is very clear. We want a cease to hostilities—as you’ve seen in the parliamentary statement; as you’ve seen from the joint Prime Ministers’ statements for Australia, New Zealand, and Canada; and as you’ve seen for our support for the General Assembly resolution.
specificity.explanation: Points to three identifiable documents (the parliamentary statement, the trilateral leaders' statement, the General Assembly resolution), which is checkable, but supplies no detail on the preconditions question actually raised.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Does he stand by his Government’s decision to repeal fair pay agreements, the Reserve Bank dual mandate, and the Clean Car Discount under urgency with no select committee process or regulatory impact statement, or does he agree with Chris Bishop that “This is a disgraceful way to make important law.”?
specificity.explanation: Names three specific repeals, the specific procedural omissions, and a directly quoted statement by a named Minister. Entirely checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Does the Government now support the immediate humanitarian ceasefire it voted for at the United Nations General Assembly yesterday, or does it still believe there are a list of preconditions that must be met before calling for a ceasefire?
specificity.explanation: Names the specific vote, the forum, the date and the specific alternative position, so the answer would be checkable against a known record.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Today’s GDP per capita figures show on a per person basis the New Zealand economy has gone nowhere since the start of 2021 and has gone backwards four quarters in a row.
specificity.explanation: A named series, a stated baseline period and a stated run length — precise enough that anyone could check it against the release.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’re eliminating wasteful spending, ensuring taxpayers’ money is spent well, and we’re clearing out the blockages in the economy and reducing costs on business so we can chart a course back to growth, investment, and opportunity.
specificity.explanation: A string of generic intentions — no programme is named, no figure, no mechanism and no date. Nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I note that the Boston Consulting Group study The Future is Electric found that electrification could reduce annual carbon emissions by 22 million tonnes in 2050.
specificity.explanation: Names the study, the finding, the quantity and the year — directly checkable against a published document.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Can he confirm that the percentage of New Zealand’s greenhouse gas emissions that come from the electricity generation is 5.7 percent, whereas the percentage of New Zealand’s greenhouse gas emissions that come from the energy sector is 40.6 percent?
specificity.explanation: Two precise figures against two clearly distinguished categories. A precise question is as specific as a precise answer.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Can he confirm that for the ETS alone to shift industrial process heat to electrification, the price needs to be in excess of $200 a tonne, and can he advise New Zealanders what it will do to their electricity and petrol bills at that price?
specificity.explanation: Names the instrument, the specific abatement task, a threshold price per tonne and the consumer costs at issue — a checkable, actionable question.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What is his plan to fix market imbalances in an electricity market dominated by four gentailers, which today’s Generating Scarcity 2023 report shows has stifled investment in renewable electricity generation and resulted in billions of excess dividends to shareholders, all while thousands of New Zealanders struggle to heat their homes?
specificity.explanation: Names the report, the market structure and the two quantified harms it is said to show, though the dividend figure is left as 'billions' rather than a number.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Has he suspended receiving regulatory impact statements because (a) he doesn’t like what they say, (b) he’s going to ignore them anyway, (c) he knows they’ll leak, or (d) all of the above?
civility.explanation: Every option offered imputes bad faith to the Prime Minister personally — dishonesty, indifference to advice, concealment — and the multiple-choice framing is mockery rather than argument. Short of a direct insult but no longer civil.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: And it’s not just for electricity supply now, but for all of the other activities that it’s going to be required—in transport and industry and energy, all of those other factors—and I thought the member might know that.
civility.explanation: The closing clause is condescension aimed at the questioner's grasp of her own former portfolio rather than at her argument. Short of a direct insult, but a real failure under the re-anchored scale.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The Auditor-General found that Ministers did not have enough information to be sure that decisions supported value for money, and that the Government carried out due diligence after announcements were made.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific finding of the Auditor-General's report into the shovel-ready and New Zealand Upgrade programmes.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Auditor-General's December 2023 report on the New Zealand Upgrade Programme and shovel-ready (Infrastructure Reference Group) projects; true if the report finds Ministers lacked sufficient information on value for money and that due diligence followed announcements, false if it makes no such finding.

veracity.statement: In the case of Auckland Transport, announcements were made about Auckland Transport projects and Auckland Transport were not even asked for the business cases or for information about the projects they were responsible for.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Auckland Transport projects were announced without AT being asked for business cases or project information.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Auditor-General's report on the NZ Upgrade/shovel-ready programmes, section covering Auckland Transport; true if it records that AT was not asked for business cases or project information before announcements, false if it records that AT was consulted.

veracity.statement: In one of the most surprising findings of this deeply troubling report, key stakeholders like the Infrastructure Commission and Auckland Transport had to find out about the New Zealand Upgrade programme through media coverage—and if that isn’t reflective of the priorities of the last Government, I’m not sure what is.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Infrastructure Commission and Auckland Transport learned of the NZ Upgrade programme from media coverage rather than from the Government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Auditor-General's report's account of stakeholder consultation on the NZ Upgrade Programme; true if it records that the Infrastructure Commission and Auckland Transport first learned of the programme through media coverage, false if it records prior notification.

veracity.statement: The advice to Cabinet noted that the transport sector remains on target to achieve its contribution to the first emissions reduction plan.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the content of the 4 December Cabinet advice: that transport remains on track for its first emissions budget contribution.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The 4 December 2023 Cabinet paper and accompanying regulatory impact statement on the Clean Car Discount, once proactively released; true if the advice states the transport sector remains on target for its first emissions reduction plan contribution, false if the advice states otherwise or is silent.

veracity.statement: In fact, the advice I’ve received shows that of the $290 million paid in tax under the ute tax scheme, half of it has come from people buying utes.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a total of $290 million collected in Clean Car Standard/Discount fees and that half of that came from ute purchases.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA Clean Car Discount fee revenue data by vehicle type to December 2023; true if total fees are about $290 million and roughly half is attributable to utes, false if either figure is materially different.

veracity.statement: In fact, I was very pleased to see yesterday that Ford announced that, from 1 July, the day after the tax will be removed, they will be reducing the price of some of their electric vehicles from between $5,000 and $8,000.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Ford has announced price reductions of $5,000–$8,000 on some of its electric vehicles timed to the removal of the fee.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ford New Zealand's December 2023 pricing announcement; true if Ford announced reductions of $5,000–$8,000 on some EV models, false if no such announcement was made or the reductions are materially different.

veracity.statement: If the Government is concerned about subsidising wealthy people, why is the Government happy to give money—billions of dollars in tax breaks—to wealthy landlords when that does nothing to reduce emissions?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Government is giving billions of dollars in tax breaks to landlords.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury/IRD costing of the restoration of interest deductibility for residential rental property as announced in 2023; true if the fiscal cost is in the billions over the forecast period, false if it is materially less.

veracity.statement: The 2022 Programme for International Student Assessment results released last week found that half of students said learners get distracted by using devices in every, or most, math lessons compared to 30 percent of students on average in the OECD.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two figures from PISA 2022 on device distraction in maths lessons: about 50 percent for New Zealand against an OECD average of 30 percent.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The OECD PISA 2022 results (Volume II) tables on digital device distraction in mathematics lessons; true if the New Zealand figure is about 50 percent and the OECD average about 30 percent, false if either differs materially.

specificity.statement: In the case of Auckland Transport, announcements were made about Auckland Transport projects and Auckland Transport were not even asked for the business cases or for information about the projects they were responsible for.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific organisation, the specific documents (business cases) and the specific process failure — checkable against the report.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We are committed to multi-generational infrastructure up and down this country, but we also know that proper process and respect for taxpayer money should be at the forefront of our decisions, and it will be under this coalition Government.
specificity.explanation: Trying to convey a governing intention but supplies no figure, mechanism, project or timeframe — 'multi-generational infrastructure' and 'proper process' commit to nothing checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: In fact, the advice I’ve received shows that of the $290 million paid in tax under the ute tax scheme, half of it has come from people buying utes.
specificity.explanation: Gives a dollar total, a proportion and the vehicle class it applies to — checkable against the fee data.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Why won’t he release the draft regulatory impact statement that was prepared by the Ministry of Transport on the impacts of carbon emissions before we vote on the legislation today?
specificity.explanation: Names the exact document, the agency that produced it, its subject matter and the deadline that makes it relevant — a precise question, as checkable as a precise answer.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Does the official advice that the Minister is refusing to release before we vote on the legislation concur with the report released by Concept Consulting for Drive Electric that the reduced uptake of electric vehicles, because of the repeal of the Clean Car Discount, will see New Zealand spending over a billion more on imported oil from overseas and mean that we will import 100,000 fewer electric vehicles in the period from now to 2030, thereby increasing carbon emissions relative to if the scheme stayed in place?
specificity.explanation: Names the report, its commissioner, two quantified outcomes ($1 billion, 100,000 vehicles) and the period they apply to.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The 2022 Programme for International Student Assessment results released last week found that half of students said learners get distracted by using devices in every, or most, math lessons compared to 30 percent of students on average in the OECD.
specificity.explanation: Names the study, the year, the exact measure and both comparison figures.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: That is why, as part of our 100-day plan, the Government will ban cellphone use during the school day for students so they can focus on their learning.
specificity.explanation: Names the measure, the scope (the school day, all students) and a timeframe via the 100-day plan; missing the enforcement mechanism and exemptions.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: It is clear Ministers were too worried about hitting “send” on press releases rather than ensuring value for money for taxpayers.
civility.explanation: Imputes bad faith and vanity as the motive for ministerial decisions rather than engaging the decisions themselves; sneering, though short of a direct personal insult.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: It is clear Ministers were too worried about hitting “send” on press releases rather than ensuring value for money for taxpayers.
focus.explanation: Attached to a named programme and a named accountability failure (value for money), so it is scrutiny rather than tribalism, but the weight of the sentence is a characterisation of the other side's motives.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Has the Minister received reports about past examples of Ministers adamantly refusing to release correspondence about related matters to the transport portfolio that might be in the public interest to release?
focus.explanation: No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named — the question exists only to point at an opponent's past conduct, in a debate where the clean car discount repeal was squarely available to engage.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Why won’t he release the draft regulatory impact statement that was prepared by the Ministry of Transport on the impacts of carbon emissions before we vote on the legislation today?
focus.explanation: Entirely about the measure before the House and the advice underpinning it; no party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: And I suggest that if the Opposition have a further supplementary, they should take that opportunity, but I suggest that they probably won’t.
focus.explanation: No policy, figure or outcome — purely a jibe about the other party's willingness to ask questions, in an answer where the cellphone ban was there to be discussed.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: In one of the most surprising findings of this deeply troubling report, key stakeholders like the Infrastructure Commission and Auckland Transport had to find out about the New Zealand Upgrade programme through media coverage—and if that isn’t reflective of the priorities of the last Government, I’m not sure what is.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about a real policy process, but it leaps from one consultation failure to a general conclusion about a government's whole set of priorities — a hasty generalisation from a single datum.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: In fact, I was very pleased to see yesterday that Ford announced that, from 1 July, the day after the tax will be removed, they will be reducing the price of some of their electric vehicles from between $5,000 and $8,000.
rigor.explanation: Answers a modelled projection of reduced EV uptake with a single manufacturer's price announcement — one anecdote offered against an aggregate forecast, which does not support the conclusion that uptake will not fall.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If the Government is concerned about subsidising wealthy people, why is the Government happy to give money—billions of dollars in tax breaks—to wealthy landlords when that does nothing to reduce emissions?
rigor.explanation: A tu quoque: an inconsistency between two of the Government's policies is offered as if it settled whether repealing the clean car discount is right. It engages real policies, but the inconsistency does not bear on the conclusion.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: New Zealand schools that have banned cellphone use, and overseas jurisdictions that have imposed bans, report better concentration and engagement in class, and have seen an improvement in achievement and wellbeing.
rigor.explanation: Offers evidence for the policy, but it is self-reported and correlational — schools that chose to ban phones reporting improvement does not establish that the ban caused it, and no counterfactual is offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: Does the official advice that the Minister is refusing to release before we vote on the legislation concur with the report released by Concept Consulting for Drive Electric that the reduced uptake of electric vehicles, because of the repeal of the Clean Car Discount, will see New Zealand spending over a billion more on imported oil from overseas and mean that we will import 100,000 fewer electric vehicles in the period from now to 2030, thereby increasing carbon emissions relative to if the scheme stayed in place?
divination.explanation: Relays a third-party forecast that repealing the Clean Car Discount will cost over $1 billion in extra imported oil and result in 100,000 fewer EV imports by 2030.
divination.subject: other
divination.falsification_criterion: NZTA/Ministry of Transport light electric vehicle registration statistics 2024–2030 compared against the Ministry's pre-repeal uptake projections, plus MBIE oil import data; true if cumulative EV imports fall short of the pre-repeal projection by roughly 100,000 and oil import spend exceeds it by over $1 billion, false if uptake tracks or exceeds the pre-repeal projection.

veracity.statement: Exports hit a high of $57.7 billion this year but are forecast to drop to $54.3 billion in the year to June 2024.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that food and fibre export revenue reached $57.7 billion in the year just ended, as reported in the December 2023 Situation and Outlook for Primary Industries report.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MPI Situation and Outlook for Primary Industries (December 2023) reported food and fibre export revenue for the year to June 2023; true if it states $57.7b (± rounding), false if materially different.

veracity.statement: Non-tariff barriers cost New Zealand agriculture around $8 billion each year.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific annual cost of non-tariff barriers to New Zealand agriculture.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MFAT / MPI published estimates of the cost of non-tariff barriers to New Zealand primary exports; true if a published official estimate is around $8b per year, false if the official estimates are materially different or no such estimate exists.

veracity.statement: The sector accounts are 81.9 percent of New Zealand’s goods exports to the year June 2023.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the food and fibre sector's share of New Zealand goods exports for the year to June 2023 was 81.9 percent (spoken slip for 'accounts for').
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MPI SOPI / Stats NZ goods export figures for the year ended June 2023; true if the food and fibre share is 81.9% (± rounding), false if materially different.

veracity.statement: Has he asked any questions about the fiscal risk or cost of not meeting our 2030 carbon budget and the potential penalties from the EU, given that our free-trade agreement (FTA) with the EU specifies that we will be taking action, and if we are not seen to be taking serious action to meet our 2030 commitments, there will be penalties under that FTA.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the NZ–EU free-trade agreement commits New Zealand to climate action and provides for penalties if it is not seen to be acting to meet its 2030 commitments.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The text of the NZ–EU FTA trade and sustainable development chapter and its dispute-settlement provisions; true if the agreement binds the parties to Paris/2030 climate commitments and allows trade sanctions or equivalent remedies for non-compliance, false if climate obligations are non-binding or excluded from enforcement.

veracity.statement: Because we know from the Climate Commission report that was released the day before yesterday that the Climate Commission has provided evidence and a recommendation to the Government that there needs to be a specific step taken to deal with the upfront cost barriers of purchasing a lower- or zero-emissions vehicle.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the He Pou a Rangi Climate Change Commission report released on or about 10 December 2023 recommends specific action to address the upfront cost barrier to buying low- and zero-emissions vehicles.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Climate Change Commission advice published in December 2023; true if it contains a recommendation that the Government address upfront cost barriers to low/zero-emission vehicle purchase, false if no such recommendation appears.

veracity.statement: That is that from 2025 to 2030, we need to see our annual light electric vehicle (EV) registrations climb from 11 percent to 67 percent of the market, and reach 100 percent by 2035.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Climate Change Commission's demonstration pathway requires light EV registrations to rise from 11% to 67% of the market between 2025 and 2030, and to 100% by 2035.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Climate Change Commission's demonstration path figures for light EV registration share; true if the 11%/67%/100% milestones for 2025/2030/2035 match, false if the published pathway gives materially different shares or dates.

veracity.statement: Of course, that requires the evidence that is in the public domain—that requires an ETS pricing of $235 a tonne, which will have around an 80c a litre, or more, impact on the price of petrol.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that publicly available evidence puts the ETS price needed to drive the EV switch at $235 a tonne, and that this equates to roughly 80c or more per litre of petrol.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Climate Change Commission / MfE modelling of the emissions price required for the demonstration path, and the standard conversion from carbon price to petrol price (about 2.4c per litre per $10/tonne); true if a published source gives ~$235/tonne and the arithmetic yields ~80c/litre, false if the sourced price or conversion is materially different.

divination.statement: Exports hit a high of $57.7 billion this year but are forecast to drop to $54.3 billion in the year to June 2024.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that food and fibre export revenue will fall to $54.3 billion in the year to June 2024.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: MPI SOPI actual food and fibre export revenue for the year ended June 2024; true if the outturn is at or near $54.3b (within about 2%), false if it lands materially above or below.

focus.statement: We have stopped Labour’s war against farmers.
focus.explanation: Characterises the other party's general disposition toward farmers; no measure, figure or outcome is named, so there is no policy content to engage with.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Has he asked any questions about the fiscal risk or cost of not meeting our 2030 carbon budget and the potential penalties from the EU, given that our free-trade agreement (FTA) with the EU specifies that we will be taking action, and if we are not seen to be taking serious action to meet our 2030 commitments, there will be penalties under that FTA.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure before the committee: it names the 2030 carbon budget, the fiscal risk of missing it, and a specific consequence under a named trade agreement. This is scrutiny of a named commitment, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’ll be working to get costs down; better rules, not more regulations; supercharge the rural economy so farmers can be proud of what they do.
specificity.explanation: A string of generic intentions — no figures, no named rule changes, no timeframe, nothing anyone could check or act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Yes, and, in particular, actions to repeal Labour’s inequitable and fiscally irresponsible ute tax by 31 December as part of our coalition Government’s hundred-day plan.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific measure being repealed and a firm date (31 December), tied to a named programme; checkable, though no amounts or mechanism are given.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: That is that from 2025 to 2030, we need to see our annual light electric vehicle (EV) registrations climb from 11 percent to 67 percent of the market, and reach 100 percent by 2035.
specificity.explanation: Three figures, a defined metric (annual light EV registrations as a share of the market) and two dates — fully checkable against the pathway she cites.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Of course, that requires the evidence that is in the public domain—that requires an ETS pricing of $235 a tonne, which will have around an 80c a litre, or more, impact on the price of petrol.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the policy: if the ETS is the sole switching mechanism, the carbon price needed implies a petrol price effect. The step from 'the modelling shows this price would be required' to 'this is the Government's chosen lever' is a gap — it attributes an intention that follows from the modelling only if the Government accepts that price path.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I think, given that we are not going through a select committee process and given that the House is not being released all the information that the Minister holds in the form of the regulatory impact statement, this committee of the whole House has a responsibility to understand the information that the Minister had there.
rigor.explanation: Two stated premises — no select committee stage, and the regulatory impact statement withheld — support the conclusion that the committee of the whole must do the scrutiny instead. The inference holds; the unstated step is that scrutiny must happen somewhere, which is assumed rather than argued.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Is it correct that the New Zealand Health Survey shows that the smoking prevalence for Māori is still 17 percent, and repealing amendments to the Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products Act will mean unacceptable levels of Māori cancers and Māori deaths, and aren’t those outcomes worth showing some moral courage for?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the New Zealand Health Survey records Māori smoking prevalence at 17 percent at the time of speaking.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The New Zealand Health Survey 2022/23 adult daily-smoking prevalence for Māori; true if the published figure is approximately 17 percent, false if materially different (e.g. below 15 or above 20 percent).

veracity.statement: What does he say to the thousands of people who marched, the 47,000 who signed a petition, and the 67 percent of voters who want our smoke-free laws to stay, and why won’t he front up to them?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 47,000 people signed a petition to retain the smokefree laws and that 67 percent of voters want them kept.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Parliament petition record (or the organising group's published signature count) for the 2023 petition to retain the smokefree legislation, and the published public poll cited for the 67 percent figure; true if both numbers match the sources within rounding, false if either is materially overstated.

veracity.statement: Could I ask the Minister whether or not eight New Zealanders with Māori in their background in Cabinet is not evidence enough of equality and democratic representation in this country?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that eight members of the current Cabinet are of Māori descent.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The November 2023 Cabinet list against published records of ministers' Māori whakapapa; true if eight or more Cabinet ministers (as distinct from ministers outside Cabinet) are of Māori descent, false if the count is lower.

veracity.statement: I’m absolutely proud of there being the highest number of Māori members in the Cabinet that there ever has been.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that this Cabinet contains more Māori members than any previous New Zealand Cabinet.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Counts of Cabinet ministers of Māori descent across previous New Zealand Cabinets, in particular the 2020-2023 Labour Cabinet; true if the November 2023 count strictly exceeds every prior Cabinet, false if any earlier Cabinet equalled or exceeded it.

veracity.statement: Today I am pleased to announce that my bill to repeal the fair pay agreements system has passed its third reading in Parliament.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Fair Pay Agreements Act Repeal Bill completed its third reading on the day of the statement.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Parliament bill record and Hansard third-reading division for the Fair Pay Agreements Act Repeal Bill; true if the third reading is recorded as taken and passed on 12 December 2023, false if it occurred on a different date or had not yet occurred.

veracity.statement: First, I want to make it clear that no worker will have their wages cut or be worse off, because no fair pay agreements were finalised.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that no fair pay agreement had been finalised at the time of the repeal.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MBIE's record of fair pay agreement bargaining as at December 2023; true if no agreement had been ratified or brought into force, false if any had been finalised.

specificity.statement: Is it correct that the New Zealand Health Survey shows that the smoking prevalence for Māori is still 17 percent, and repealing amendments to the Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products Act will mean unacceptable levels of Māori cancers and Māori deaths, and aren’t those outcomes worth showing some moral courage for?
specificity.explanation: Names the data source, gives a figure, and names the specific Act whose amendments are to be repealed. Checkable and actable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: This Government is committed to reducing smoking rates and helping people quit smoking.
specificity.explanation: A statement of general commitment with no mechanism, target, figure or timeframe; nothing in it could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Particular areas of need we’re targeting are shorter stays in emergency departments, faster cancer treatment, improved immunisation, shorter wait times for first specialist assessment, and shorter wait times for surgery.
specificity.explanation: Names five distinct target areas, which is real content, but supplies no thresholds, baselines or dates — the 'how much' and 'by when' are absent.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What does he say to the thousands of people who marched, the 47,000 who signed a petition, and the 67 percent of voters who want our smoke-free laws to stay, and why won’t he front up to them?
specificity.explanation: Carries two precise figures — a petition count and a polling percentage — that someone could go and verify.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Why is the Minister proposing to repeal a structure that will enable Te Aka Whai Ora to take a local approach empowering hapū, iwi, and whānau through iwi-Māori partnership boards and localities?
specificity.explanation: Names the entity and two concrete delivery mechanisms (iwi-Māori partnership boards, localities), but offers no funding, coverage or timing detail.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Does the Minister think that repealing section 7AA of the Oranga Tamariki Act, disestablishing the Māori Health Authority, repealing smoke-free legislation, removing Māori names of Government departments, repealing fair pay agreements, and introducing a Treaty Principles Bill will enhance the Māori-Crown relationship, and, if so, will he and the Prime Minister be prepared to front up and discuss this at Waitangi 2024?
specificity.explanation: Enumerates six named measures, one down to the statutory section, plus a named occasion and date. Every element is checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What does she say to the 200,000 to 300,000 workers who would’ve benefited from fair pay agreements?
specificity.explanation: Carries a stated numeric range tied to a named policy, which is checkable against coverage estimates, though the basis of the range is not given.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Next week, I will be introducing a bill to the House to expand access to 90-day trials to employers.
specificity.explanation: Names the instrument, the mechanism being changed and a timeframe. Missing only the detail of which employers and by what threshold.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Is it correct that the New Zealand Health Survey shows that the smoking prevalence for Māori is still 17 percent, and repealing amendments to the Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products Act will mean unacceptable levels of Māori cancers and Māori deaths, and aren’t those outcomes worth showing some moral courage for?
civility.explanation: The substance is squarely about the policy, but the closing clause imputes a want of moral courage to the Minister personally rather than contesting his reasoning.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I find it interesting with that member, who was part of a Government that took a wrecking ball to our health system in the middle of a pandemic.
civility.explanation: 'I find it interesting' is sneering, and the remark is directed at the member's association rather than at any argument she made — short of a direct insult but no longer civil.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Could I ask the Minister, will he set time aside in the discussion or kōrero at Waitangi, for Willie Jackson to explain why he lost all those Māori seats?
civility.explanation: A jibe framed as a question, aimed at a named member's personal electoral failure rather than at anything he argued. Mockery of the individual, not the position.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Can he confirm that, following this flip-flop, the Government’s health policy amounts to nothing but scrapping the free prescriptions initiative in order to fund cancer medicines while allowing more cancer-causing tobacco to fund millionaire’s tax cuts?
focus.explanation: Names three real measures (free prescriptions, cancer medicines funding, tobacco law) but frames them through 'millionaire's tax cuts' party framing rather than engaging the mechanism.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I find it interesting with that member, who was part of a Government that took a wrecking ball to our health system in the middle of a pandemic.
focus.explanation: Gestures at the previous government's health restructure but names no measure, figure or outcome; the weight of the remark is on who the member is rather than on any policy.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Why is the Minister proposing to repeal a structure that will enable Te Aka Whai Ora to take a local approach empowering hapū, iwi, and whānau through iwi-Māori partnership boards and localities?
focus.explanation: Entirely about the measure before the House — the repeal of a named statutory structure and the delivery mechanism it creates. No party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: If he agrees that iwi and Māori are best placed to ensure our health system works well for Māori at a central level as well as through local devolution, then why not ensure this is resourced through Te Aka Whai Ora that was already established, instead of creating a new model?
focus.explanation: Engages the substance directly: whether an existing named body should be resourced rather than replaced. No content about the other party as such.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Does he acknowledge that removing the smoke-free laws will mean more people will die from smoking while the only people who will benefit from this are landlords getting tax cuts?
focus.explanation: The first half is a genuine policy claim about the repeal's health effect; the second half — 'the only people who will benefit are landlords getting tax cuts' — is party framing carrying most of the rhetorical weight.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Does the Minister think that repealing section 7AA of the Oranga Tamariki Act, disestablishing the Māori Health Authority, repealing smoke-free legislation, removing Māori names of Government departments, repealing fair pay agreements, and introducing a Treaty Principles Bill will enhance the Māori-Crown relationship, and, if so, will he and the Prime Minister be prepared to front up and discuss this at Waitangi 2024?
focus.explanation: Legitimate scrutiny: names specific government measures and asks about their effect on a specific relationship. Holding a minister to account for named commitments is on-policy.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Could I ask the Minister, will he set time aside in the discussion or kōrero at Waitangi, for Willie Jackson to explain why he lost all those Māori seats?
focus.explanation: Entirely about an opponent's electoral fortunes. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Can he confirm that, following this flip-flop, the Government’s health policy amounts to nothing but scrapping the free prescriptions initiative in order to fund cancer medicines while allowing more cancer-causing tobacco to fund millionaire’s tax cuts?
rigor.explanation: Reduces an entire health policy programme to three chosen items with 'amounts to nothing but' — a hasty generalisation, and the causal link asserted between tobacco revenue and tax cuts is offered without support.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If he agrees that iwi and Māori are best placed to ensure our health system works well for Māori at a central level as well as through local devolution, then why not ensure this is resourced through Te Aka Whai Ora that was already established, instead of creating a new model?
rigor.explanation: A clean conditional: it grants the Minister's own stated premise about who is best placed and draws the institutional consequence from it. The gap is that it assumes the existing body is the only vehicle for that premise.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Could I ask the Minister whether or not eight New Zealanders with Māori in their background in Cabinet is not evidence enough of equality and democratic representation in this country?
rigor.explanation: Non sequitur: the descriptive composition of one Cabinet is offered as sufficient evidence of 'equality and democratic representation' in the country at large. Nothing connects the ministerial headcount to the general conclusion.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: National-led Governments have linked in and engaged with many Māori over time, including in Waikato, with the Waikato River settlement. That is a great reflection of working together.
rigor.explanation: Generalises from a single cited instance to a claim about a pattern of engagement over time — an argument from anecdote, with no other evidence offered to support the general conclusion.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Repealing the fair pay agreements legislation gives businesses the certainty they need to invest and grow, creating more and better jobs.
rigor.explanation: A three-step causal chain — repeal produces certainty, certainty produces investment, investment produces more and better jobs — asserted with nothing offered at any link. Bare assertion rather than inference.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Secondly, Māori, Pasifika, young people, and women will not be harmed or made worse off by the repeal of the fair pay agreements, because no fair pay agreement was finalised.
rigor.explanation: Equivocates on 'worse off': the premise establishes only that no existing entitlement changes, but the conclusion is about harm generally, which would include the loss of prospective gains from bargaining already under way. The conclusion is broader than the premise supports.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: Does he acknowledge that removing the smoke-free laws will mean more people will die from smoking while the only people who will benefit from this are landlords getting tax cuts?
divination.explanation: Forecasts that repealing the smokefree amendments will produce additional smoking-related deaths relative to what would otherwise have occurred.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: New Zealand Health Survey adult daily-smoking prevalence and Ministry of Health smoking-attributable mortality series after the December 2023 repeal; true if smoking prevalence or smoking-attributable deaths depart upward from the pre-repeal downward trend, false if the decline continues at or above the pre-repeal rate.

veracity.statement: As I’ve answered numerous times—and I’m not sure if it’s actually relevant to Part 2 in relation to the question of the carbon impact, but I’ll answer it anyway—as I’ve said, advice I’ve received shows that this does not impact on our ability to meet the carbon budget for the 2025 period, and that is something I’ve answered.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that official advice received by the Minister concludes the repeal of the Clean Vehicle Discount does not affect New Zealand's ability to meet the emissions budget covering the 2025 period.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Ministry of Transport advice and the regulatory impact statement for the Land Transport (Clean Vehicle Discount Scheme Repeal) Amendment Bill, plus Climate Change Commission / MfE emissions-budget projections for the first emissions budget (2022–2025); true if that advice states the first budget is still met after repeal, false if the advice projects the budget being exceeded as a result.

veracity.statement: They had a marginal abatement cost per tonne of between minus $170 and $199.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific published figure: that the Clean Car Discount was assessed as having a negative marginal abatement cost in the range of about minus $170 to minus $199 per tonne of CO2 abated.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The cost-benefit analysis and regulatory impact statement published with the Clean Car Discount legislation (Ministry of Transport, 2021); true if the marginal abatement cost per tonne stated there falls in the cited negative range, false if the published figure is positive or materially outside minus $170 to minus $199.

rigor.statement: This adds no value as we’re discontinuing the scheme. We don’t support that tabled amendment.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion assumes what is in dispute: the amendment's whole purpose is to display the foregone rebate value after the scheme ends, so 'the scheme is being discontinued' cannot by itself show the disclosure adds no value. Question-begging.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Obviously, we don’t support that, because it’s not within the Government’s policy intent.
rigor.explanation: The only reason offered against extending the scheme is that it conflicts with the Government's own stated intent — an appeal to its own authority rather than any argument about the merits of a six-year extension.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: One of the things that we do know is that in other jurisdictions where you have had increased uptake of electric vehicles (EVs)—so usually one of the triggers of getting rid of a rebate scheme is actually that you get to price parity between an EV and an internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicle, so that the need for there to be assistance is no longer necessary, because there isn’t that delta in terms of the capital expenditure.
rigor.explanation: A coherent conditional inference about the policy: a subsidy exists to close a capital-cost gap, so once parity is reached the rationale falls away. The gap is that she establishes the principle from 'other jurisdictions' without showing where New Zealand sits on it, so the implied conclusion that this repeal is premature is not fully carried by what is offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But what I would say is that the changes that are being made here simply are to revoke the regulation which requires that the label includes information about the Clean Vehicle Discount, because, of course, this repeals that legislation.
specificity.explanation: Names the exact regulatory change (revoking the labelling requirement that discloses the Clean Vehicle Discount) and its cause; a reader could check the instrument. No figures or dates, which caps it below the top.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: It does seek to in clause 26 insert a new part within the Schedule, and that relates to an ability to have a purchase arrangement in place, Minister, by the end of 31 December 2023, and if that is the case, then the rebate would still be applicable.
specificity.explanation: Names the clause, the mechanism (a purchase arrangement triggering eligibility), and a hard cut-off date of 31 December 2023. Actionable and checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I would like to hear from the Minister an understanding of the proportion of fees and rebates that are paid and received by rural communities, and what is the proportion of fees and rebates that are paid and received by urban communities—noting that many in rural communities drive Leafs, not simply utes; noting that many in urban communities drive Ford Rangers and other large vehicles that are a danger to children on bikes.
specificity.explanation: Asks for a defined, checkable statistic — the rural/urban split of Clean Car Discount fees and rebates — and names specific vehicle models, but supplies no figures of his own and no threshold for what the answer would show.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: They had a marginal abatement cost per tonne of between minus $170 and $199.
specificity.explanation: A named metric with a numeric range and units per tonne, traceable to a specific published analysis. Whether the figure is right is a separate question.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: You know, all the evidence seems to suggest that that will narrow over time.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the purchase-price gap between electric and non-electric vehicles will shrink in the years after December 2023.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Average new and used EV versus ICE purchase prices in New Zealand (Motor Industry Association registrations data and NZTA/Trade Me price series) comparing 2023 with the resolve-by year; true if the average EV–ICE price gap in comparable segments is smaller, false if it is unchanged or wider.

civility.statement: So, to the Minister, please, can I have an answer, or will you continue to dodge?
civility.explanation: 'Continue to dodge' imputes deliberate evasion to the Minister personally rather than criticising the answer given. Short of a direct insult, but it attributes bad faith to the person, which is a genuine failure on the re-anchored scale.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If we can influence the market so that we’re selling lower-emissions vehicles here in New Zealand, we’re bringing in, we’re importing, more low- and zero-emissions vehicles. That means that we’ll have reduced emissions over a long period of time, and, as the Hon Megan Woods was just saying, of course that has a positive economic benefit for New Zealanders because they’re spending less money on fuel.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the measure before the House: given the earlier premise that a vehicle bought now locks in ~20 years of emissions, shifting the mix of imported vehicles does follow through to lower long-run fleet emissions, and lower fuel spend follows from that. The chain is coherent and the steps are connected rather than asserted; it leans slightly on the unstated assumption that the discount actually changes purchasing decisions.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: I don’t know if the Minister is aware—but he might be interested to know, especially with his portfolios—that currently our imports of vehicles and fuel to run them exceed the value of our exports in dairy.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand's combined annual import bill for vehicles plus the fuel to run them is larger than its total dairy export earnings.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ overseas merchandise trade statistics for the year to 2023: sum the import value of motor vehicles/parts and of crude plus refined petroleum, and compare with the export value of milk powder, butter and cheese. True if the combined import figure exceeds dairy exports; false if dairy exports are the larger figure.

veracity.statement: That’s why fuel is not in the ETS in Europe and I would be totally fine with fuel being taken out of the ETS here if it meant we could have a policy that was more effective like the Clean Car Discount.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that transport fuel is not covered by the European emissions trading scheme. (The second half of the sentence is the speaker's own preference and is not the checkable part.)
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The scope of the EU Emissions Trading System as at December 2023 (EU ETS Directive 2003/87/EC as amended in 2023). True if road transport fuel was outside the operative EU ETS at that date; false if road transport fuel was covered by an operating EU emissions trading scheme.

veracity.statement: The other question was in regards to other jurisdictions, and I just would like to note that the New South Wales Labour Government is ending subsidies for electric vehicles (EVs) on the same date that we will be ending subsidies on EVs.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New South Wales is ending its electric vehicle subsidies on the same date New Zealand is ending the Clean Car Discount.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The NSW Government's announced end date for its EV rebate scheme, compared with the end date of New Zealand's Clean Car Discount under this bill. True if the two dates coincide (or differ by no more than a day); false if they differ materially.

veracity.statement: And a big part of how New Zealand is going to meet emissions budget 1 is because of the reduction in transport emissions, largely driven by the uptake in electric vehicles that the Clean Car Discount has brought around.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a causal attribution: that meeting emissions budget 1 is substantially due to transport emissions falling, and that this fall is largely caused by Clean Car Discount - driven EV uptake.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry for the Environment / Climate Change Commission reporting on the composition of emissions reductions counting towards the first emissions budget. True if transport, and EV uptake attributable to the Clean Car Discount within it, accounts for a large share of the reduction; false if the reduction is predominantly attributable to other sectors (e.g. electricity generation, industrial process changes) with transport a minor contributor.

veracity.statement: But if the Minister is saying that on 1 January the Government is planning to raise the emissions trading scheme price, the unit price, to $235 a tonne, then I think New Zealanders probably need to know because when they’re coming back from their summer holidays, they’ll be paying around 80c a litre more for their gas.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that an ETS unit price of $235 a tonne would translate into roughly 80 cents a litre more at the pump than motorists were paying at the time.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Apply the standard petrol emissions factor (~2.3 kg CO2e per litre) to an ETS unit price of $235/tonne and compare the result against the pass-through at the ETS price prevailing in December 2023 (~$70/tonne). True if the increment is around 80c per litre; false if it is materially different (e.g. nearer 40c).

veracity.statement: Again, we haven’t had an opportunity to hear from people about what they think about this bill as part of the parliamentary process, and so I would be grateful if the Minister could turn his mind to those questions.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the bill reached the committee of the whole House without any stage at which the public could give its views.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Parliament's record for the Land Transport (Clean Vehicle Discount Scheme Repeal) Amendment Bill. True if the bill had no select committee stage and no public submissions were called for; false if it was referred to a select committee and submissions were heard.

veracity.statement: It’s still on the emissions reduction plan, but in the area of light vehicles, light fleet, and the potential—well, not the potential but also—so the target from the emissions reduction plan was to increase zero-emissions vehicles to 30 percent of the light fleet by 2035.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific numerical target and date drawn from the emissions reduction plan.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The transport chapter of New Zealand's first Emissions Reduction Plan (May 2022). True if it sets a target of zero-emissions vehicles reaching 30 percent of the light fleet by 2035; false if the figure or the year differs.

veracity.statement: We can link that target to the Climate Change Commission’s advice released just this week, which shows that the emissions trading scheme alone is insufficient to substantially move people away from fossil fuel - powered vehicles.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific finding of a specific, recently published Climate Change Commission document.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Climate Change Commission's advice published in the week of 11 December 2023 on the second emissions reduction plan. True if it concludes that ETS pricing alone will not deliver the required shift away from fossil-fuelled vehicles and that complementary measures are needed; false if it concludes the ETS alone is sufficient.

divination.statement: I think they’re going to be very unhappy when they realise how much costs have inflated compared to the prices that they put in their manifesto for those so-called “roads of national significance”, which are really roads of private greenfields-developer significance, particularly in the Auckland region.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the cost of the announced roads of national significance programme will turn out to be far higher than the figures the incoming government put in its manifesto.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Published NZTA/Treasury cost estimates for the roads of national significance programme, compared against the costings in National's 2023 transport manifesto. True if the official estimates materially exceed the manifesto figures; false if the programme is costed at or below the manifesto figures.

civility.statement: I note the Hon Julie Anne Genter continues to ask questions about her tabled amendment. I’ve already said we don’t support it.
civility.explanation: Pointed and dismissive — "continues to ask" frames the member as repetitive rather than engaging the amendment's merits — but it stops short of imputing bad faith or attacking her personally.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But if the Minister is saying that on 1 January the Government is planning to raise the emissions trading scheme price, the unit price, to $235 a tonne, then I think New Zealanders probably need to know because when they’re coming back from their summer holidays, they’ll be paying around 80c a litre more for their gas.
specificity.explanation: Carries a date, a unit price and a per-litre consequence — $235 a tonne, 1 January, roughly 80c a litre. Anyone could take those numbers away and check or act on them, which is what this attribute asks.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But my question to the Minister is whether he is comfortable that the time frame for the administrative functions in terms of winding things up that might come post 31 December 2023, if this bill is enacted—whether that is sufficient; whether he has received any advice relating to whether there might be a need to delay that somewhat or have some provision within Part 2, or indeed within Schedule 2, that might provide an opportunity if things were not winding up by the particular time in question; that there was provision around that.
specificity.explanation: A precise question is as specific as a precise answer: it names the date the scheme closes, the part and schedule of the bill at issue, and the exact contingency it wants addressed. It stops short of the top only because it does not say how much administrative time it thinks is required.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What then is the actual plan and the vision for moving people to the solutions and supporting our communities and our people, moving to the way that the world is going to have to adapt rather than clinging with desperation to an old world with old energy and dirty energy?
specificity.explanation: After the concrete target named a moment earlier, this reverts to generalities — "the solutions", "supporting our communities", "the way that the world is going to have to adapt". No mechanism, figure, instrument or timeframe is named, so there is nothing here anyone could check or act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: For clarity, the amendment seeks to, in clause 26, in new Part 7 of Schedule 1 of the Land Transport Act, add new clause 28 after clause 27.
specificity.explanation: Names the exact clause, Part, Schedule and Act the amendment operates on — a listener could locate and check it precisely.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The policy intention of the legislation is for the rebate and ute tax scheme to end at midnight on 31 December 2023.
specificity.explanation: Names the schemes and gives an exact time and date for their end; directly checkable against the bill and actionable for anyone buying a vehicle.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So, for example, the energy economy, if you look under the energy economy side, next to the star label, it says its cost per year is an estimate based on a petrol price of $2.50 per litre, an electricity price of 15c per kilowatt hour and an average driving distance of 14,000 kilometres.
specificity.explanation: Three exact parameters — fuel price, electricity price and annual distance — quoted from the Schedule's label; anyone could check or recompute from this.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: So while members opposite may wish that, actually, we don’t tease these out and the Minister doesn’t respond—which is their prerogative—I do think that members of the public all around the country will be expecting to know if they are going to purchase an electric vehicle that would be eligible for the rebate scheme.
focus.explanation: A genuine policy point — eligibility for the rebate scheme at the cut-off date and what buyers need to know — but framed through what 'members opposite may wish', which carries part of the weight.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I’m interested in why he’s saying it’s at midnight on 31 December 2023, because of course the Schedules refer to the close of 31 December 2023, and if the close is to mean midnight, I think it should say midnight.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure before the committee: the drafting mismatch between the Minister's stated 'midnight' and the Schedule's 'close of 31 December 2023'. No party content at all.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: This was what the Government campaigned on.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that repeal of the Clean Vehicle Discount Scheme was a policy the governing party put to voters at the 2023 election, rather than a post-election decision.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: National's 2023 general election transport/climate policy documents and campaign statements: true if the party publicly committed before the October 2023 election to repealing the Clean Car Discount (and the associated 'ute tax'); false if no such pre-election commitment can be found.

veracity.statement: I’m just wondering if the Minister can tell us if there’s provision for the information that’s used to calculate the estimated cost to change, based on rising petrol prices, because petrol prices have been over $2.50 a litre, I think, for quite a while, and they stay above $2.50.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand retail petrol prices had been, and remained, above the $2.50 per litre figure used in the Schedule's energy label.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MBIE weekly retail fuel price monitoring for 91 octane petrol over 2022–2023: true if the national average pump price sat above $2.50 per litre for most of that period up to December 2023; false if it was at or below $2.50 for most of it.

rigor.statement: So, if anything, this label, if it’s using $2.50 per litre as the estimate, is underestimating the cost savings of an energy-efficient vehicle.
rigor.explanation: Valid inference: if actual petrol prices exceed the $2.50 assumption, a savings estimate built on that assumption must understate the saving. The conclusion follows from the premise offered; no fallacy or gap.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: This will be a short contribution, and I note that these new MPs across from us are very full of themselves.
civility.explanation: A personal characterisation of the members opposite — their self-regard, not their argument or their policy. Nothing of the bill is engaged in the remark.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: As I look ahead, I know we need so much more than faux indignation and misplaced guilt that makes us paralysed from making progress.
civility.explanation: A contested political passage where she had a real opportunity to be uncivil. She imputes insincerity ('faux indignation') and misplaced motive to unnamed opponents, which is edging past robust disagreement into bad faith — but no individual is named or attacked, so it stays above a personal attack.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I see the task ahead is to show leadership in how we respect and accommodate difference while getting on with the job of finding practical solutions and not commentating on the problems.
specificity.explanation: A statement of governing intent that is trying to convey substance, but carries no figure, mechanism, timeframe or named policy — a string of generic virtues ('practical solutions', 'accommodate difference') that nobody could check or act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: I descend from Tapua, whose children were Tari, Patuone, and Tamati Waka Nene, the latter both being chiefs who signed Te Tiriti o Waitangi and, in so doing, became part of building the nation we now enjoy.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific genealogical and historical fact: that Tapua's children included Tari, Patuone and Tamati Waka Nene, and that Patuone and Tamati Waka Nene were both signatories to Te Tiriti o Waitangi.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Te Tiriti o Waitangi signatory sheets (Archives NZ / the Waitangi Tribunal's published signatory lists): true if both Eruera Maihi Patuone and Tamati Waka Nene appear as signatories, false if either does not. Genealogy checked against Te Ara / Dictionary of New Zealand Biography entries for Patuone and Nene naming their father as Tapua.

veracity.statement: Very early in my career, I was a delegate for the Police Association, advocating for better conditions and protections for my police family—eventually being elected by my peers as vice-president, working in that role with one of your Assistant Speakers, Greg O’Connor.
veracity.explanation: A claim about her own record: that she served as a New Zealand Police Association delegate and was elected vice-president of the Association, serving alongside Greg O'Connor.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police Association records, annual reports or contemporaneous Police News issues listing office-holders: true if Costello appears as an elected vice-president during a period overlapping O'Connor's tenure as president, false if she held no such office.

civility.statement: The reason why that’s an appropriate title is because all of the things that are contained in all of the clauses within this bill lend themselves to stupid types of decisions—decisions that are not going in any direction to support households and communities to look at their emissions profile and to make some real positive decisions in that space.
civility.explanation: Harsh language ('stupid types of decisions') aimed squarely at the bill's clauses and the decisions they produce, not at any member. Under the re-anchored scale, brutal criticism of a policy sits near the top; the mild deduction is for 'stupid' characterising the decision-making rather than arguing about it.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The reason why that’s an appropriate title is because all of the things that are contained in all of the clauses within this bill lend themselves to stupid types of decisions—decisions that are not going in any direction to support households and communities to look at their emissions profile and to make some real positive decisions in that space.
rigor.explanation: There is a real inference here about the measure before the committee — the clauses do nothing for household emissions, therefore the proposed title fits — but the premise is bare assertion. Nothing in the clauses is identified, and the pejorative 'stupid' stands in for the supporting reason. Closest to an appeal to characterisation in place of evidence.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Yes, there is some sense to that, but it also, I think, needs to be considered alongside other campaign commitments which were not campaigned on but suddenly are making their way through at some stage to become laws—and, you know, we think of things like smoke-free generations.
rigor.explanation: A genuine rebuttal to the Minister's mandate justification rather than a jibe: if the 'we campaigned on it' principle is not applied to other measures (smokefree generations), the justification carries less weight. The inference is relevant and names a comparator, but nothing is offered to establish that the two measures are alike in the relevant way, so it leans on a tu quoque.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The reason why that’s an appropriate title is because all of the things that are contained in all of the clauses within this bill lend themselves to stupid types of decisions—decisions that are not going in any direction to support households and communities to look at their emissions profile and to make some real positive decisions in that space.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure: the bill's clauses, their effect on household and community emissions. No party framing at all. High focus alongside low rigor is the intended combination — arguing weakly about a real policy is still on-policy.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I think that the suggestion of replacing that 1 January 2024 with 1 January 2025 is very helpful, and I hope that members will be supportive of both of those clause changes.
